Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Georges Perrot (author, Wikidata Q1281062), died 1914; Charles Chipiez (author, Wikidata Q1281019), died 1901; Walter Armstrong (translator, Wikidata Q7964171), died 1918. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Perrot, Georges, 1832-1914; Chipiez, Charles, 1835-1901; Armstrong, Walter, Sir, 1850-1918 [Translator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: A History Of Art In Chaldaea And Assyria Vol-Ii, 1884, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/AHistoryOfArtInChaldaeaAndAssyriaVolII. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 95%, 94%, 87% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Georges Perrot, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
